Shelagh Powell is a prominent figure in Danish child and adolescent psychiatry, serving as the chairperson of the steering group for the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] [^src2]. In this capacity, she plays a central leadership role in the strategic governance and quality monitoring of ADHD treatment across Denmark [^src1]. 

Professionally, Powell is employed as a chief physician (*overlæge*) at [[bua|Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Afdeling (BUA)]], specifically within Team 2 for school children's psychiatry [^src1]. This department is part of [[aarhus-universitetshospital-psykiatrien|Aarhus Universitetshospital, Psykiatrien]] in the Central Denmark Region (Region Midtjylland) [^src3]. She also represents the Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Society in Denmark (*Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Selskab i Danmark*) and is associated with the [[bua-psykiatrisk-klinik-for-skoleboern|BUA Psykiatrisk Klinik for Skolebørn]] [^src3]. Her work intersects with the broader national efforts to evaluate and improve ADHD treatment quality, addressing systemic challenges such as waiting times, IT infrastructure, and regional disparities in patient pathways highlighted in the database's annual reports [^src2].
